subject: Onboarding: Clearport benchmarking & acceptance plan
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Handoff: Clearport onboarding - benchmark targets and next steps

Diego / Marcus team —

Quick handoff for Clearport (deal CP-2026-042). They finished API integration on Monday and CS has scheduled the implementation kickoff for next week. Clearport is asking for a benchmark window this month to validate latency and throughput before we flip traffic. High level:

- Target p95 latency: <= 120ms for 512-token requests (chat endpoint)
- Target throughput: sustained 300 req/s with 50ms inter-request jitter
- Tail: p99 target <= 450ms

Attachments: customer-provided traffic profile (they shared a spreadsheet). Samira at Clearport is the engineering lead — looped below. Please confirm the test script and the data/telemetry we need to collect so CS can schedule the 2-hour test window.

Acceptances/asks:
- Marcus: confirm whether we run on dedicated pool or hosted with burst capacity.
- Neha: prepare a perf test script and set of telemetry assertions.
- Diego: coordinate run window and post-test artifacts for the customer-facing sign-off doc.

Thanks —
Monica
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: clearport-load-schedule-20260618.xlsx (XLSX)

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira.khan@clearport.com>, DevOps <devops@clearport.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Handoff: Clearport onboarding - benchmark targets and next steps

Thanks Mon — taking point.

Plan I propose:
1) Run in Dedicated pool (reserve 2x expected capacity) — Marcus, can you confirm a 4-GPU pool on g5dn-equivalents for the run? If not, we'll fallback to hosted + burst.
2) Test schedule: Thu 2026-06-24 16:00-18:00 PT (customer requested either 24th or 25th).
3) Workload: start with baseline 50 rps, ramp to 300 rps over 20 minutes, hold 300 rps for 60 minutes, then ramp down. Include short bursts at 450 rps for 2 x 5-minute windows to validate tail behavior.
4) Telemetry: token-level cost, per-request latency (client-observed), server-slot queuing, GPU utilization, KV cache hit ratio.

Neha — can you produce a k6 script and a short runbook by EOD Monday? Samira — please confirm that the token lengths we should test are 128/512/1024 and whether you want context-cold vs warm cache runs.

Diego
Implementation Lead | Redwood Inference

> On Thu, Jun 18, 2026 at 09:12 AM Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com> wrote:
> > Diego / Marcus team —
> > ...

From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@clearport.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: DevOps <devops@clearport.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 12:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Handoff: Clearport onboarding - benchmark targets and next steps

Thanks — quick clarifications from our side:

- Confirmed token lengths: 128 (quick lookup), 512 (common chat flow), 1024 (long-form). Please prioritize 512 as representative.
- We prefer two test windows: one for warm cache (to show steady-state) and one cold-start (after cache flush) — can you schedule both during the 2-hour block?
- We'll provide a synthetic request set reflecting peak product flows (checkout + fraud check + chat). Attaching the traffic profile we referenced.

Also, our compliance team wants a copy of the telemetry schema you will export (latency fields, timestamps, anonymized request id) so they can ingest into our observability.

Samira Khan
Engineering Lead, Clearport
Attachment: clearport-traffic-profile.csv (CSV)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira.khan@clearport.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Handoff: Clearport onboarding - benchmark targets and next steps

Attached is the initial perf pack: a k6 script, a telemetry mapping, and a checklist for the run. Highlights:

- Script: clearport-k6-script.js (parameterized for token sizes 128/512/1024, warm/cold toggles).
- Acceptance assertions (automated): p95 <= 120ms for 512 tokens AND error rate < 0.5% over steady-state window. If assertions fail we capture 10 minutes of full request/response traces for triage.
- Telemetry schema: fields we will provide — request_id, start_ts, end_ts, client_observed_ms, server_process_ms, queue_ms, gpu_util_pct, cache_hit (bool), model_version. We'll deliver as NDJSON. Link to sample: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bClearportOnboard

Runbook (summary):
1) 15m warmup at 50 rps
2) 20m ramp to 300 rps
3) 60m steady 300 rps with two 5m 450 rps bursts at minutes 20 and 40
4) 10m cool-down

I'll be on the 24th to run and monitor. Marcus — can you confirm pool sizing and whether we should pin the model variant (quantized) for cost predictability?

Neha Kapoor
Perf Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachment: clearport-k6-script.js (JS)
Attachment: clearport-latency-summary-20260615.csv (CSV)

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@clearport.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Handoff: Clearport onboarding - benchmark targets and next steps

Perfect — thanks team. Final confirmations and next steps:

- Test window locked: Thu 2026-06-24 16:00-18:00 PT (both warm and cold runs within that block).
- Resources: Marcus confirmed 4x g5dn-equivalent GPUs reserved during the run. We'll pin model:v2-quant (quantized) unless Clearport requests otherwise.
- Acceptance criteria (customer-facing): p95 <= 120ms (512 tokens), p99 <= 450ms, sustained 300 req/s, error rate < 0.5%. If pass, CS will move to phased traffic cutover. If fail, we will produce a triage report within 48 hours with remedial actions.
- Deliverables to customer within 24 hours of run: run-summary.pdf (pass/fail), raw telemetry NDJSON, and a short executive note with cost estimates for steady-state.

Samira — let us know if you want a pre-run smoke test on the 23rd for 15 minutes; we can do that at 10:00 PT.

Diego
Implementation Lead | Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: run-summary-template.docx (DOCX stub referenced for post-run)
